## The Checklist

* *Phase 1*: Convergence Diagnostics
* *Phase 2*: Posterior Predictive Checks
* *Bridge*: Variance partitioning with intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) & global year trend (spline)
* *Phase 3*: Results & Inference

## Phase 1: Convergence Diagnostics

Check if the MCMC chains actually finished their job.

* R-hat
* Effective Sample Size (ESS)
* Trace plots
* Density plots
* Lag plots

```{r Phase1_setup, include=FALSE}
invisible(capture.output(source("13_MetaAnalysis_Diagnostics.r", local = TRUE)))

fit_obj <- if (exists("ebf_fit.upd")) ebf_fit.upd else ebf_fit
fit_summary <- as.data.frame(fit_obj$BUGSoutput$summary)
fit_summary$parameter <- rownames(fit_summary)

ess_vals <- coda::effectiveSize(as.mcmc(fit_obj))
ebf_mcmc <- as.mcmc(fit_obj)

diag_overview <- tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Maximum R-hat",
    "Median R-hat",
    "Minimum ESS",
    "Median ESS",
    "Parameters with R-hat > 1.01",
    "Parameters with ESS < 400"
  ),
  Value = c(
    round(max(fit_summary$Rhat, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    round(median(fit_summary$Rhat, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    round(min(ess_vals, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    round(median(ess_vals, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    sum(fit_summary$Rhat > 1.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(ess_vals < 400, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

flagged_rhat <- fit_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Rhat) & Rhat > 1.01) |>
  dplyr::select(parameter, Rhat)

flagged_ess <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = names(ess_vals),
  ESS = as.numeric(ess_vals)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(ESS < 400)

flagged_diag <- flagged_rhat |>
  dplyr::full_join(flagged_ess, by = "parameter") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Rhat), ESS)

if (nrow(flagged_diag) == 0) {
  flagged_diag <- tibble::tibble(Message = "No monitored parameters exceeded thresholds.")
}

trace_params <- c("prev_global", "sigma_country", "sigma_district", "sigma_region")
trace_params <- trace_params[trace_params %in% varnames(ebf_mcmc)]

density_params <- c("prev_global", "sigma_country", "sigma_district", "sigma_region")
density_params <- density_params[density_params %in% varnames(ebf_mcmc)]
```

```{r Phase1_summary, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf(
  "The model converged: maximum R-hat = %.3f and minimum ESS = %s across all monitored parameters.\n\n",
  round(max(fit_summary$Rhat, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
  format(round(min(ess_vals, na.rm = TRUE), 0), big.mark = ",")
))
```

```{r Phase1_overview}
# Convergence overview table — kept here in the DIAGNOSTIC output only.
# It is deliberately NOT repeated in the manuscript Results Section (§3.2),
# which shows the one-line convergence statement instead.
knitr::kable(diag_overview, caption = "Convergence overview") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r Phase1_flagged}
knitr::kable(flagged_diag, digits = 3, caption = "Flagged convergence parameters") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r Phase1_traceplots, fig.height=8}

  coda::traceplot(ebf_mcmc[, trace_params, drop = FALSE])
}
```

```{r Phase1_densityplots, fig.height=8}

  lattice::densityplot(ebf_mcmc[, density_params, drop = FALSE])
}
```

## Bridge: Variance partitioning with intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)

Answers the question: “Of all the reasons why two random EBF surveys in my dataset are different, what proportion of that difference is because they come from different studies, districts, countries, or regions?” The latent study mean ($\theta_i$) is retained in the model as a random effect; residual study-level variance (`tau_study`) is reported separately and is not part of the geographic variance decomposition.

```{r ICC_setup, include=FALSE}
invisible(capture.output(source("15_MetaAnalysis_ICC.r", local = TRUE)))
```

```{r ICC_table}
icc_display <- as.data.frame(icc_table) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Level") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    median = round(median * 100, 1),
    lower  = round(lower * 100, 1),
    upper  = round(upper * 100, 1)
  )

knitr::kable(icc_display, caption = "Variance decomposition (%)") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r ICC_plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
print(icc_plot)
```

### Global year trend (B-spline)

The model includes a cubic B-spline on year of prevalence (`r spline_meta$N_KNOTS` interior knots, quantile-placed, `r spline_meta$N_spline_cols` basis columns) to absorb the global time trend in EBF rates. Spline coefficients are given an independent shrinkage prior ($\beta_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\text{spline}})$) to prevent overfitting in years with sparse survey coverage. Because the latent study mean ($\theta_i$) absorbs study-level noise, the spline reflects the underlying structural time trend rather than being pulled toward individual outlier surveys. The plot below shows the posterior median and 95% credible interval of the global EBF trend, evaluated at the grand mean prevalence.

```{r Bridge_spline_trend, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
print(year_trend_plot)
```

Once Phases 1 and 2 are acceptable, we move to the substantive results.

* Posterior Summary plots: forest, caterpillar, and half-eye plots
* Exceedance (Target) Probabilities
* Exceedance (Relative-Region) Probabilities

#### Exceedance (Target) Probabilities

```{r Phase3_target}
knitr::kable(league_table, caption = "Global ranking and target probabilities") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

print(target_plot)
```

#### Relative-Regional Performance

```{r Phase3_relative, results='asis', fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
for (rg in region_levels_present) {
  cat("\n\n### Relative-regional performance:", region_label(rg), "\n\n")
  print(relative_plot.f(rg))
  print(relative_sum.f(rg))
}
```

At the end of the analysis we can provide three distinct layers of insight:

* **Absolute Performance:** which country has the highest posterior EBF prevalence
* **Relative Performance:** whether a country is outperforming its region
* **Target Confidence:** how likely a country is to have met the WHA 50% target (2025 goal); the more ambitious 60% target (WHO/UNICEF, 2030 goal) is also reported
